cues.text: Hi, Greg. How did it go with the research on renewable energy? Have you found anything?
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Yes. But I think it’s about time we exchange our findings and discuss our next move.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: You read my mind. Right. I’ll start first. Germany is the very first country I dug into in order to find innovative means of creating clean energy because 15% of its national electricity supply conies from renewable sources.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: I found that apart from the traditional fossil fuel industry, there’s a German firm that has initiated a project using kites to generate power.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Really, I’ve never heard of it before. How does it work?
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: As a substitution for traditional fossil fuels that release toxic gas into the atmosphere, the power-generating kites can function in any weather.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Compared to conventional wind turbines, such kites can produce twice as much energy because the overall power density is proportional to altitude.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Sounds like an efficient way of producing power. Okay, now let me tell you what I have found.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: There is an American company manufacturing school buses and city buses depending solely on electricity instead of gasoline.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: The all-electric vehicles can save up to 20 gallons of fuel on a daily basis.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: This could reduce transport budgets by over $10,000 each year, not to mention maintenance savings.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: Wow, impressive. If only there were more of these electric vehicles around.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Well, over the years, South Africa has attached great importance to clean energy.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: The nation encourages using propane gas, which can either be extracted from natural deposits or be produced organically.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: It is normally stored in gas canisters as a type of cooking gas. To reduce the number of kitchen accidents, a new type of composite gas canister made of fiber was introduced.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: It is much safer and less likely to explode even when engulfed in fire.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: Now, about the survey, do you have any clues as to what kind of interviewees we should include?
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: How about local companies doing business on clean energy products?
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Probably not the best choice of respondents.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: Remember the last time we asked corporate employees tc do the questionnaire, only about 5% of them were actually willing to participate.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: That wouldn’t be enough then. It seems we have to drop that idea.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Then maybe we can ask the professors and administrative staff here to help us.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: They could provide their insights and understanding on energy production.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: It would be ideal if they would, but I’m afraid most of them are too busy to respond to the list of questions we’ve prepared.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: I guess the students here at the university would be more suitable.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: You’re right. And it is a much bigger sample pool too.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Also, I think we should include the locals. Their opinion is key to the promotion of renewable energy here in the town.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: But wouldn’t it be difficult to collect data? There’s no way the two of us could go from door to door to interview all the residents.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: There’s no need to worry about that. We’ll make it telephone interviews. That way we’ll have enough time to get sufficient data.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Good idea. What should we present in our speech?
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: Due to lack of media coverage, the majority of people actually have a limited understanding on renewable energy.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Most of them aren’t able to identify various types of renewable sources.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: So I feel we could start by clarifying what it is and the benefit of it compared to fossil fuels.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: That makes sense. We could start with wind energy.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: For centuries, wind has been used to do work. With the help of windmills, farmers used to pump water from wells or turn large grinding stones to grind wheat or corn.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: The windmills today generate electricity. The only problem is that it might not be windy all the time, so it is crucial to choose the appropriate site for wind farms.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: Well, I think we can also include comparisons between clean energy and traditional energy resources like coal, oil and natural gas.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Maybe we can look into the prospect of these conventional sources of energy.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: The rising cost of fossil fuels and the threat of climate change is a concern to many
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: Totally. These traditional resources will deplete eventually.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Renewable energy currently makes up less than 2% of the world’s primary energy supply, and although growing very rapidly, it is not on course to fill the fossil fuel gap.
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Nuclear energy is another type of energy we ought to mention. Nuclear power plants can produce dependable power constantly and release far less greenhouse gases than other traditional power plants.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: But most people feel that this type of energy is unsafe because radiation isn’t easily dealt with, especially in nuclear waste and maintenance materials
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: What should we end the speech with?
cues.speaker: Syria

cues.text: Have you heard about a new type of energy called hydrogen fuel?
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: It is an infinitely renewable fuel that doesn’t have detrimental environmental effects.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: The only problem is that it is so expensive that only wealthy individuals can afford it.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: But I think overall the benefits overshadow its high cost.
cues.speaker: Greg

cues.text: I think that even though this new type of renewable energy is too expensive to use at the moment, in the long run, its price will go down and become more accessible.
cues.speaker: Syria
